concepts.title: Pressure Belts and Winds: Planetary Circulation
concepts.definition: Atmospheric circulation begins with the equatorial low, subtropical highs, subpolar lows and polar highs, and the surface winds of trade winds, westerlies and polar easterlies, with the Coriolis force deflecting winds and the ferrel cell and polar cells completing the tricellular model.
concepts.key_idea: The intertropical convergence zone shifts with the overhead sun, bringing seasonal wind reversals that underlie the monsoon circulation.

concepts.title: Air Masses, Fronts, Cyclones and Anticyclones
concepts.definition: Air masses acquire the character of their source regions, meet at fronts of warm, cold, stationary and occluded types, and give birth to mid-latitude cyclones with rain belts, while tropical cyclones form over warm seas with spiral rain bands and a calm eye, and anticyclones bring clear settled weather.
concepts.key_idea: Tropical cyclones need sea temperature above 27 degrees, coriolis force and low level convergence, and they die over land or cold water.

concepts.title: Monsoon Circulation and Seasonal Wind Reversal
concepts.definition: The monsoon is a seasonal reversal of winds caused by differential heating of land and sea and the shift of the ITCZ, bringing rain-bearing winds to Asia in summer and dry offshore winds in winter, and it is the most important regional weather system on the earth.
concepts.key_idea: Summer heating of Asia draws moist equatorial air inland giving heavy rains, while winter high pressure over the continent reverses the flow.
